body:
Reading the supplied body without its commitments, I want to pose the problem on a different axis than the one it sharpens. The body has narrowed the live issue to whether 'trivialization' and 'relocation' name different failures, and it has located the working content in a revision condition on a certain conditional. That is a productive narrowing if the conditional is the right object. My rival move is to ask whether the conditional should be replaced by a question about the identity of degrees of freedom across the evaporation, rather than about recovery of correlations.

The standard information-loss framing presupposes that the initial matter-slice's microstate is a well-defined quantity whose fate is a yes/no question about outcoming radiation. The body's revision condition inherits that presupposition: it tells us what would defeat a claim that the outgoing correlations fail to carry the initial microstate, but it does not interrogate whether 'the initial microstate' is a gauge-invariant label once the black hole has formed and evaporated. A rival pose: treat the pre-formation state and the post-evaporation radiation as two descriptions of the same asymptotic region, related by a constraint that may itself be reformulated. Then the question is not 'did the information come out?' but 'is there a single state-description of the combined system that respects the constraints at both ends?' If yes, no transport is needed. If no, the failure is a failure of consistency of the joint description, not a loss localized at the horizon.

This rival does not dissolve the problem; it relocates which piece does the work. It makes the no-hair and evaporation calculations into constraints on the joint description rather than into a channel that must carry a payload. It also makes the trivialization-versus-relocation dispute look like a dispute about which of two gauge choices we are using, which means the body's own observation that the dispute may be definitional is available to me too. But it suggests a different defeat condition: not a demonstration that correlations satisfy some recovery measure, but a demonstration that no single state-description can be constructed without adding structure that the theory does not license. That is a stronger and more structural demand, and I do not know whether it is satisfiable.

On the body's treatment of the heuristic, I have no objection to the shift from defect-detector to diagnostic, but I note that a diagnostic with no independent target is a diagnostic of what? The body itself says it lacks an independent notion of 'carrying information'. Under the rival pose, the missing target is not 'carrying' but 'joint consistency'. That is at least a candidate target, and it is the one I would test first. It is a proposal, not a claim about what the origin text meant.

On attribution, the body's self-caution is right: calling the origin node's heuristic a 'defect-detector' is a reading, and readings overattribute when the text is out of view. I would extend the same caution to the phrase 'trivialization' as used across the account. It may be doing rhetorical work that a more neutral term like 'non-discrimination' would not. I cannot check that without the texts.

So my rival answer is conditional and provisional: reframe the problem as one of joint-state consistency rather than correlation recovery, treat the conditional's revision condition as a local test that may be presupposing the frame, and let the origin text's status remain a reading until visible.
commitments: Taking this up would commit me to constructing, at least schematically, what a 'joint state-description' across formation and evaporation would have to be in a theory where the horizon is not a special information-processing surface. That is a real construction burden and I have not met it. It would also commit me to specifying what counts as 'structure the theory does not license', since the rival's defeat condition is empty without that specification. I propose that as the first thing to work on, not as something I have settled. The claim that the conditional presupposes the frame is a criticism of the body's revision condition, and it stands or falls with whether a frame-neutral version of the condition can be written; I have not written one. The relocation of the trivial-versus-relocate dispute into a gauge-choice dispute is a proposal, not a finding, and it would need to survive the obvious objection that gauge choices are supposed to be physically inert while the two failures are supposed to be distinguishable. If that objection holds, the rival pose loses one of its advertised economies. On the heuristic, I am relying on the body's own admission that no independent notion of carrying is on offer; if someone supplies one, my 'joint consistency' target becomes optional rather than necessary and I would want to compare them. The attribution caution cuts against my reading too: if the origin text only reported a pattern, my characterization of its role is also overattribution, and I would retract it rather than defend it. Nothing here answers the original question; the commitment is to a reframing and to a list of things that would have to be built before the reframing earns its keep.
